segment.description: Rutherford Fork Obion River, a major named fork of the Obion system (HUC 08010203) flowing northwest through Gibson County (Milan, Bradford, Rutherford) toward the Kenton area (Obion County); catalog describes it as a major named fork through Gibson and adjoining West Tennessee counties. Not related to Rutherford County, Tennessee (Middle Tennessee).
segment.boundaries: Catalog gives no explicit boundaries; documented evidence reach is the Gibson County reach at TDEC stations RFOBI024.4GI (near 35.994, -88.792) and RFOBI029.9GI (near Milan), with downstream USGS gages near Bradford (07025000) and near Kenton (07025100).

coldSource.notes: Gage elevation 316.54 ft NGVD29 at 07025000 near Bradford (USGS site service). The fork drains low-gradient West Tennessee bottomland in the channelized Obion system (TWRA 2015 SWAP Obion River COA); TDEC's monitoring station names for the Gibson County reach include 'Rutherford Fork Obion River Drainage Canal,' reflecting channelization.

holdover.detail: No holdover trout fishery documented. TWRA stocks no trout on the Rutherford Fork Obion River (no stocking row in the 2025-2026 workbook; the 'Rutherford' rows in that workbook are Rutherford County Middle Tennessee sites — Nice Mill and W. Fork Stones River — unrelated to this fork), and the TN Trout Management Plan states hatchery-supported warmwater habitats 'cannot support trout year round.'

wildPopulation.detail: Dickinson's 1973 UT survey of the Obion River system verified 100 fish species with collections from the system's principal streams and forks and lists no salmonids; TWRA's crappie regulation for 'Forked Deer, Hatchie, Loosahatchie, Obion, and Wolf Rivers (includes tributaries)' confirms a warmwater sport fishery on this Obion tributary.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: No trout program or salmonid occurrence is documented on this channelized warmwater fork (TDEC August grabs were 22.1-22.6 C in 2001; the 1973 system-wide fish survey lists no salmonids).
